findings.title: Non-canonical YouTube media_ref makes the whole artifact fail validation instead of being ignored
findings.explanation: The new check `(data.media_refs || []).some((ref) => ref?.provider === "youtube" && !validYouTubeRef(ref))` throws "Invalid YouTube source reference." for the entire artifact. `validYouTubeRef` requires an exact match: `view_url === "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>"`, an 11-char `video_id`, and `time_unit === "seconds"`. Before this release the viewer had no YouTube handling at all, so such a ref was simply ignored and the graph still rendered. Now any deviation (a `youtu.be` short URL, an extra query parameter, a `watch` URL with different casing/order, a missing or differently spelled `time_unit`) hard-fails `validateThreadsArtifact`, which is shared by local file open, `?src=<url>`, the authenticated Drive path, and the new public Drive path. This is a stricter, whole-artifact-fatal contract than the rest of the validator (which tolerates unknown fields) and couples artifact viability to one exact string produced only by the still-unfinished companion importer. No supported-input regression is proven (the real exported artifact and the importer's canonical output pass), so severity is low, but an adversarial reading is that invalid media metadata should be dropped/flagged while still rendering nodes/edges, rather than blocking the viewer entirely.
findings.reproduction: Open a local `.threads` file whose graph_data/edges are valid but whose media_refs contains `{ "provider": "youtube", "video_id": "6HmR9IaqM88", "view_url": "https://youtu.be/6HmR9IaqM88", "time_unit": "seconds" }` (or omit `time_unit`). `validateThreadsArtifact` throws "Invalid YouTube source reference." and ThreadsViewer shows an error with no graph, whereas the same file minus the media_ref (or on the base commit) renders normally.
